properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 27 at 10:04AM CDT until August 28 at 10:20AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

White River at Hazleton.

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Mount Carmel.

.Minor flooding continues along the lower White River at Hazleton and
should come to an end by Friday morning. Minor flooding also
continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down to Mount Carmel
with the crest approaching Mount Carmel. Flooding should come to an
end on the Wabash during the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...White River at Hazleton.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Lowest reading available from the Hazleton
Staff Gage.  Since the 1930s the White River has moved from the
"old wellhouse" to several hundred yards from the "old wellhouse".
The river returns to the "old wellhouse" around 17 to 17.5 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is no current observed data.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 5.4 feet Sunday, September
06.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM CDT /1215
AM EDT/.

substructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural

ground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year
round.

- At 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Thursday the stage was 20.1 feet.

at 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Thursday was 20.1 feet.

this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

San Isabel, Highway 165, Beulah, Highway 78, stream crossings, and
county roads within and immediately downstream of the burn scar.

and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.
properties.instruction:

Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Move away and to higher ground immediately.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 27 at 7:14PM EDT until August 27 at 10:30PM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
At 714 PM EDT, trained weather spotters reported flash flooding in
Muncy Valley. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hughesville, Muncy Valley, Lairdsville and Picture Rocks.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
